agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider closing road portions at 722 Gore Avenue for a new park
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will vote on November 17, 2026 on a resolution to close, stop-up and raise title to a 0.286-hectare portion of road at 722 Gore Avenue (Block 121, District Lot 196, Plan 13098, dedicated in 1968) and designate it permanent public park under section 488(5)(a) of the Vancouver Charter. The closure follows Reference Plan EPP155773 prepared by Elliot Perley, B.C.L.S., completed September 29, 2026. The motion is subject to Council first approving Report 4. Requests to speak must be received before 5 pm on November 16, 2026.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Submit a request to speak to Council at vancouver.ca/speak-to-council before 5 pm on November 16, 2026 if you want to address the road closure.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider rezoning 1125 West 10th Avenue to CD-1
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider a bylaw that would change the zoning of 1125 West 10th Avenue to CD-1. CD-1 is a site-specific zone, meaning Council writes rules for that one property instead of using the citywide rules. The change would allow a different kind of building or use than the current zoning permits. Several councillors must first review the meeting record before they can vote on it. If approved, the new rules would apply only to this address.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Yaletown BIA expansion up for Council consideration in 2027
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider expanding the Yaletown BIA to include seven commercial properties on Marinaside Crescent (folios 159-607-88-0363 to -0369, addresses 1079–1097), occupied by a bakery and café, a pet food retailer, and a veterinary clinic. The BIA's existing term (April 2024–March 2029) and levy ceiling stay unchanged. If approved, the City will notify affected owners and businesses, forward the request to a Court of Revision hearing, and report back in February 2027. Council cannot approve the expansion if most property owners oppose it and they represent more than half the area's assessed property value.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Business Licence Hearing Panel assignments for late 2026
agenda_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council will consider delegating business licence hearings and appeals under the Vancouver Charter to three-member Council panels on four dates: November 24 and 25, and December 8 and 9, 2026, all at 9:30 am. Each panel has a designated chair and an alternate; if a member cannot attend, the remaining two councillors plus the alternate decide. The panels hear cases where a licence is refused, suspended, or has conditions attached.

minutes_briefs.title: Council voted to explore City support for Land Trust purchase of three SROs
minutes_briefs.summary: Council voted unanimously to direct staff to look at ways the City could help the Downtown Eastside Community Land Trust buy three single-room occupancy (SRO) buildings: The Arlington (575 East Pender Street), The York (259 Powell Street) and The Laurel (610 Alexander Street). Staff will study partnerships with senior government and a possible capital grant, and report back to Council by the end of January 2027. key_dates.label: Vancouver staff report on SRO acquisition support due to Council

minutes_briefs.source_body: A. THAT Council direct staff to report back on options for how the City could support The Downtown Eastside Community Land Trust (“Land Trust”) in acquiring The Arlington (575 East Pender Street), The York (259 Powell Street), and The Laurel (610 Alexander Street), including exploration of partnership with senior government and a potential capital grant contribution to support the acquisition, with a report back for Council’s consideration no later than the end of January 2027. B. THAT Council direct staff to urgently send a letter to the Land Trust outlining Council’s decision but making clear that the Council resolution in support of this exploration in no way binds Council to any particular decision when staff report back at the end of January 2027. C. THAT Council request that the Mayor communicate with the Minister of Housing, Infrastructure and Communities Canada at earliest convenience, reflecting urgency and opportunity of acquiring these SROs. minutes_briefs.title: Vancouver Council received the 2026 local election results report
minutes_briefs.summary: Vancouver Council voted unanimously to receive the report dated October 27, 2026, titled "2026 Local General Election Results." The report was accepted for information only, meaning Council took no new action and passed no new rules. Mayor Fry was absent for the vote. The report simply records the official results of the 2026 local general election. No changes to licensing, permits, fees, or business rules were part of this decision.
minutes_briefs.source_body: THAT the Report dated October 27, 2026, entitled “2026 Local General Election Results”, be received for information. CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY (Vote No. 11968) (Mayor Fry absent for the vote)

minutes_briefs.title: Council Approved Consultation Plan for Kingsway Rezoning, Adding Renfrew-Collingwood Area Council
minutes_briefs.summary: Council voted unanimously to direct staff to consult with affected people, organizations and authorities on rezoning applications that would amend the Vancouver Official Development Plan, as listed in Appendix A of the October 27, 2026 report. Council also added the Renfrew-Collingwood Area Council to the list of groups to be consulted on the application at 3410-3436 Kingsway. Council confirmed it will provide at least one chance for public input, and that consultation can be early and ongoing.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If you own property or run a business near 3410-3436 Kingsway, watch for City consultation notices and make sure your views are submitted during the comment period.
minutes_briefs.industries: Construction & Development, Landlord & Property Mgmt, Retail
minutes_briefs.source_body: THAT Council, a. regarding proposed amendments to the Vancouver Official Development Plan for the rezoning applications by address listed in Appendix A of the Report dated October 27, 2026, entitled “Required Consultation for Rezoning Applications to Amend Vancouver Official Development Plan”; b. having considered whether the opportunities for consultation with certain persons, organizations and authorities listed in Appendix B of the above-noted report should be early and ongoing, and being aware of its obligation to provide at least one opportunity for consultation; and c. add “Renfrew-Collingwood Area Council” to the list of organizations and authorities listed in Appendix B of the above-noted report to be consulted on for the application at 3410-3436 Kingsway; directs staff to consult with persons, organizations and authorities it considers will be affected, as detailed in Appendix A of the above-noted report. minutes_briefs.title: Council approved expanding Yaletown BIA and sent it to Court of Revision
minutes_briefs.summary: Council confirmed the Yaletown Business Improvement Association (BIA) as the sponsor for an expanded Yaletown BIA and approved starting a Council Initiative to add the proposed expansion area. The BIA's existing operating term and funding ceiling stay the same. Council forwarded the BIA's application to a hearing of the Court of Revision, the independent body that hears complaints about local improvement charges. The City will notify property owners and businesses in both the current BIA and the proposed expansion area.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If your business or property is in the Yaletown BIA or the proposed expansion area, watch for the City's notice and review how the BIA levy will apply to you before the Court of Revision hearing.
minutes_briefs.source_body: A. THAT Council confirm the Yaletown Business Improvement Association as the sponsor for an expanded Yaletown BIA. B. THAT Council approve the commencement of a Council Initiative to expand the Yaletown BIA to include the proposed expansion area outlined in Appendix A of the Report dated October 20, 2026, entitled “Council Initiative – Business Improvement Area (BIA) Expansion 2027 (Yaletown),” with no changes to the BIA’s existing operating term or funding ceiling; FURTHER THAT Council forward the application of the Yaletown Business Improvement Association to a hearing of the Court of Revision. C. THAT the City notify property owners and businesses within both the existing Yaletown BIA and the proposed BIA expansion area. ADOPTED ON CONSENT (Vote No. 11977)

minutes_briefs.title: Council voted to close road at 722 Gore Avenue and make it permanent park
minutes_briefs.summary: Council voted unanimously to close, stop up and raise title to about 0.286 hectares (0.706 acres) of road at 722 Gore Avenue. "Stop-up" means legally closing the road so it is no longer public road. Council also designated the land as permanent public park under section 488(5) of the Vancouver Charter. The decision comes with terms and conditions listed in the September 22, 2026 report. The land is now park, not road.
minutes_briefs.action_required: Check whether your business uses or accesses this section of road at 722 Gore Avenue and plan for the change now that it is closed.
minutes_briefs.industries: Construction & Development, Landlord & Property Mgmt, Transportation & Logistics
minutes_briefs.source_body: THAT Council close, stop-up and raise title to that approximately 0.286-hectare (0.706 acre) portion of road at 722 Gore Avenue (the “Property”), the same as shown in Appendix A of the Report dated September 22, 2026, entitled “722 Gore Avenue – Close, Stop-up, Raise Title and Permanent Park Designation,” subject to the terms and conditions noted in Appendix B of the same report; FURTHER THAT subject to A above being approved, Council designate, pursuant to section 488(5) of the Vancouver Charter, the Property as permanent public park. minutes_briefs.title: Council delegated business licence hearings to three-member panels for late 2026
minutes_briefs.summary: Council voted to hand certain business licence hearings and appeals to panels of three Council members instead of the full Council. The panels will handle hearings under Section 275 or 278 and appeals under Section 277 of the Vancouver Charter on four dates Council set: November 24 and 25, and December 8 and 9, 2026. Each panel has a named chair, two members, and an alternate. The decision was adopted on consent (Vote No. 11976), meaning no separate recorded vote was needed. Business owners with a licence hearing or appeal on those dates will appear before a three-member panel, not the whole Council.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If you have a business licence hearing or appeal scheduled on one of these dates, confirm your hearing details with the City and prepare to present to a three-member panel.

minutes_briefs.title: Council approved changes to the Vancouver Heritage Register
minutes_briefs.summary: Council voted to amend the Vancouver Heritage Register by approving the additions, deletions and adjustments listed in Appendix A of the August 5, 2026 report called "Vancouver Heritage Register Annual Update." The register is the City's official list of buildings and sites with heritage value. Being added to it can affect what property owners can do with their buildings, including renovations and demolition. The decision passed on consent, meaning it was approved without debate.
minutes_briefs.action_required: Check Appendix A of the August 5, 2026 report to see if your property was added to or removed from the Vancouver Heritage Register, and review what that means for any renovation or redevelopment plans.

minutes_briefs.title: Council approved $101,050 in 21 community sport event grants
minutes_briefs.summary: Council approved 21 Vancouver Community Sport Event Grants totalling $101,050 from the 2026 Community Sport Hosting Program Budget. Council also approved a separate $5,000 grant to Volleyball BC for the 2026 Vancouver Open (July 10–12, 2026). Council gave the City's Director of Destination Events and Tourism authority to sign the grant agreements and pay out the money. Council also declared that any recipient that is not a registered charity counts as an organization that adds to the culture, health or welfare of the city, as the Vancouver Charter requires. No legal rights or obligations exist until each recipient signs and returns its grant agreement.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If your organization received one of these grants, sign and return your grant agreement letter to the City before spending any of the funds.

minutes_briefs.title: Vancouver Council voted to hold closed meetings on labour, land, and negotiations
minutes_briefs.summary: Council voted unanimously to go into closed meetings later this week to discuss labour relations, land deals, and early-stage negotiations. The meetings are closed to the public under Section 165.2(1) of the Vancouver Charter, which lets council meet privately on certain sensitive topics. Council cited three reasons: personal information about a current or potential city employee, labour or employee relations, and land or property deals where public disclosure could harm the city's interests. Council also cited early-stage negotiations about a proposed activity, work, or facility. No decisions from these closed sessions have been made public.
minutes_briefs.industries: Construction & Development, Labour & Employment, Landlord & Property Mgmt
minutes_briefs.source_body: THAT Council will go into meetings later this week which are closed to the public, pursuant to Section 165.2(1) of the Vancouver Charter, to discuss matters related to paragraphs: (a) personal information about an identifiable individual who holds or is being considered for a position as an officer, employee or agent of the city or another position appointed by the city; (c) labour relations or other employee relations; (e) the acquisition, disposition or expropriation of land or improvements, if the Council considers that disclosure could reasonably be expected to harm the interests of the city; (k) negotiations and related discussions respecting the proposed provision of an activity, work or facility that are at their preliminary stages and that, in the view of the Council, could reasonably be expected to harm the interests of the city if they were held in public. CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY
